note: Both exports go through the durable production job (mix/master revision -> approve -> export) on a Neon-backed local API, with the operator-local VST3 worker (services/vst3-render-worker) hosting Steinberg Retrologue 2.4.0. The Song Model is the seeded benchmark case; the arrangement was generated by ARRANGEMENT_ORCHESTRATOR and selected in the studio flow.

run1_refusal.outcome: Every stem fell back to the preview synth with the precise refusal reason; the export completed but was preview-only. Groove Agent SE, Padshop and HALion Sonic render silence without a loaded program, so their smoke failed and they were not attested.

run2_native.outcome: All three stems rendered licensed-native through Retrologue with attested provenance; the export is production-ready with 3 native stems and 0 fallbacks. This required the orchestrator to attach canonical performance evidence to performed tracks (it had been discarding it) and the export path to persist bundles through the storage client instead of the Replit sidecar.

honestLimits: Only Retrologue is attested on this workstation; the three content instruments need a saved .vstpreset before they can be attested.
Routing by family sends the bass to whatever 'strings' maps to (the bass lives in the strings definition family); role or instrument rules exist precisely so operators do not rely on family for bass.

Native stems in run 2 still carried a stale fallbackReason text from the preview pass alongside rendererStatus=licensed-native; fixed in this PR so the field is present only when a fallback actually happened.
Nobody has listened to the rendered stems; production-ready here is the export engine's evidence gate, not a musical judgement.
